scope: uncommitted working-tree diff (git diff) + untracked tests/unit/test_ip_allowlist.py; data-flow neighbours read: app/main.py, app/dependencies.py, app/routers/auth.py, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, docker-compose.windows.yml, nginx/nginx.conf, installer/core/env_writer.py, .venv uvicorn 0.29.0 proxy_headers.py

findings.message: The new ALLOWED_IPS guidance tells operators to trust uvicorn forwarded headers (--forwarded-allow-ips / FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS) but does not warn that the wildcard value turns the allowlist into a client-controlled header. Installed uvicorn 0.29.0 (.venv/Lib/site-packages/uvicorn/middleware/proxy_headers.py, get_trusted_client_host) returns x_forwarded_for_hosts[0] - the LEFTMOST, fully attacker-supplied entry - when trusted_hosts contains the wildcard, while the nginx-IP form correctly returns the rightmost untrusted entry. proxy_headers is on by default (uvicorn/config.py:203,468). Because docker-compose.prod.yml gives the nginx container a dynamic bridge IP, the wildcard is the path of least resistance for an operator locked out by the intentional fail-closed 403. Not BLOCK: no file in this repo sets the wildcard today, all admin routes still require an admin session (require_role -> get_current_admin), and with the documented per-IP value the header cannot be spoofed through nginx (it appends $remote_addr last).
findings.fix: Extend the .env.example note: state explicitly that FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS must name the proxy address and that the wildcard makes ALLOWED_IPS spoofable via X-Forwarded-For. Give a concrete recipe - pin the nginx container to a static address with an ipam block in docker-compose.prod.yml and set FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS to that address plus uvicorn --forwarded-allow-ips.

findings.message: Deployment docs are incomplete for the prod topology the change creates. nginx location /api/ proxies /api/admin/* to the app with no allow/deny restriction, and docker-compose.prod.yml:71 runs uvicorn without --forwarded-allow-ips, so request.client.host is always the nginx container address. The documented consequence is a hard 403 lockout in prod; the docs never warn that the obvious operator workaround - adding the nginx container IP to ALLOWED_IPS - silently converts the allowlist into allow-any-internet-client, because every admin request then arrives from that one trusted address. The risk is misconfiguration, not a reachable exploit in the current tree, so WARN rather than BLOCK.
findings.fix: Document (and preferably add) an nginx-level control: a dedicated location /api/admin/ block with allow <office-ip>; deny all; before proxy_pass, so the perimeter enforces the same policy independently of the app. Add an explicit NEVER line to .env.example: never list the reverse-proxy address in ALLOWED_IPS.

findings.message: The client-IP caveat is only approximately right for this repo's compose files. docker-compose.yml uses a project-scoped bridge network, so the observed gateway is normally 172.18.x.1 and not the default-bridge 172.17.0.1 given as the example. Under rootless Docker / some port drivers the published port at docker-compose.yml:73 can present the source as 127.0.0.1, which simultaneously matches the default ALLOWED_IPS=127.0.0.1 and the default FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS trust set, making X-Forwarded-For trusted for any LAN client reaching host:8000.
findings.fix: Say the gateway address is environment-specific and must be read from `docker network inspect`, and note the rootless-Docker case where the source appears as 127.0.0.1.

findings.message: The comment claims the allowlist is 'checked before admin login/role checks', but no admin login endpoint exists: admin_sub is only read (app/dependencies.py:42) and never issued anywhere in app/. The ordering claim holds for role checks (router-level dependencies are solved before route-level ones), but the allowlist covers only /api/admin/*, so an admin login added later under /api/auth/* would be outside the protected prefix.
findings.fix: Reword to 'enforced on every /api/admin/* route, before the role check', and add a note to the story that a future admin login endpoint must either live under /api/admin/ or carry require_server_ip explicitly.

findings.message: Routes declared with path '/' (users, portals, config) are reached as /api/admin/users etc. via Starlette's redirect_slashes, which issues a 307 during routing - before any dependency runs. A blocked IP therefore sees a 307 rather than a 403 on the unslashed form and can enumerate which admin route prefixes exist. Following the redirect yields 403, so no data is exposed.
findings.fix: Optional: declare the collection routes with explicit paths or set redirect_slashes=False on the app if route-existence disclosure matters.

findings.message: allowed_ip_list performs no format validation on entries - any string (hostname, typo, CIDR block, IPv6 literal) is accepted and compared by exact string equality. All failure modes are fail-closed, but an operator writing a CIDR range, a hostname, or connecting over IPv6 (::1 or ::ffff:127.0.0.1) gets a silent 403 with no diagnostic. The tests confirm this by allowlisting the literal string 'testclient'.
findings.fix: Optionally parse entries with ipaddress.ip_network and log a startup warning for unparseable entries; consider CIDR support so operators are not tempted to widen the list another way.

findings.message: A rejected admin request raises 403 without emitting an audit event, so probing of /api/admin/* from non-allowlisted addresses leaves no record in app/security/audit_log.py alongside the other admin.* events this diff preserves.
findings.fix: Emit an audit or structlog warning (event name plus the observed client host) on rejection; keep it rate-limited so it cannot be used to flood logs.

verified_no_finding: Coverage: all six /api/admin routers (config, crawls, ops, portals, taxonomy, users) carry dependencies=[Depends(require_server_ip)]; app/main.py registers no other /api/admin router and no admin endpoint exists under another prefix. tests/unit/test_ip_allowlist.py::test_every_admin_route_depends_on_require_server_ip enumerates app.routes dynamically, so a future unguarded admin router fails CI.

Fail-closed logic: 'not client_ip or client_ip not in allowed' denies empty string, None (uvicorn sets scope['client'] = (None, 0) when every X-Forwarded-For entry is trusted) and any unlisted value; allowed_ip_list drops blank entries so ALLOWED_IPS='' yields [] and denies all. A literal '*' in ALLOWED_IPS matches no IP, so there is no accidental allow-any value.

Header spoofing through the shipped topology: nginx sets X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (real client appended last) and uvicorn 0.29 returns the rightmost untrusted entry for a non-wildcard trust list; with the default FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=127.0.0.1 and no proxy trust configured, forwarded headers are ignored entirely in both compose files. Refuted as an exploitable path today - retained only as the misconfiguration WARN VULN-001.
Ordering: FastAPI prepends router-level dependencies, so require_server_ip runs before require_role/get_current_admin; the 403-without-session test confirms it.

No new injection surface: admin routers use bound parameters (taxonomy UPDATE uses :s/:cat/:id), ORM selects elsewhere; no secret is added to source or logs by this diff; app/routers/admin/config.py returns only non-secret settings.
docker-compose.prod.yml does not publish the app port, so the only route to /api/admin in prod is through nginx.
